# Start here: gtmtechweek continuation

## Objective and ownership

User: Adrian / GitHub `az2kxx`. Repository: https://github.com/az2kxx/gtmtechweek . Public dashboard: https://gtmtechweek-tender-observatory.adrian-k-zebrowski.chatgpt.site . The user expressly authorizes commits/pushes to this repo and public, login-free dashboard access.

This is a contest/demo PoC with a path to real execution. The user finds utility tenders, researches either one E2E supplier or several complementary suppliers, contacts technical/commercial owners and facilitates a technical discussion. The goal is useful technical dialogue and an eventual commercial integration/coordination mandate. No fee, partner commitment or mandate is currently agreed.

Latest instruction: public GitHub is the demo SSOT, dashboard must diagnose execution, show outstanding connections, and retain the ability to use real tools later. Keep Attio intact. No distribution integrations need activation merely to complete the PoC.

## Costs and permissions

Clay: **299 DATA credits maximum per logical flow execution**, strictly below the user's 300-credit limit. The same budget covers all tenders, branches, retries and resumes. Monthly cap was not specified. Reuse company/person field caches across tenders and channels. Begin with one relevant decision-maker per qualified company. Unknown/unbounded cost or uncertain billing units blocks the paid call. A local ledger is not an account-level billing cap and must precede every live paid dispatch.

The user permits repo writes and public demo viewing. This does not authorize ad spend, publishing through a CMS, contacting people or auto-enrolling them into outbound campaigns. Keep those operations draft/paused until separately authorized in the active host context. Attio research writes remain authorized; preserve live interaction state.

## Execution model

1. Research fresh notices using official procurement/utility sources, with a 14-day overlap; dedupe by reference/lot/version. Coverage includes electricity, water/wastewater, gas networks and district energy worldwide.
2. Record source access failures separately from no opportunities; retain deadline/timezone precision and mandatory early gates.
3. Screen E2E and consortium routes for requirement coverage, eligibility, geography and capacity. Keep inferred work packages labeled.
4. Use cached Clay data first; qualify missing roles and bound any paid call before enrichment.
5. Persist each relevant contact independently of matching. Missing counterpart gets a reason and review date; single E2E route does not need a pair.
6. Draft actor-specific email/LinkedIn offers and followups. General blog content should explain technology/use case without announcing a collaboration.
7. Commit sanitized canonical data and an evidence-based execution log; rebuild the projection. Optionally mirror research into Attio without resetting relationship history.
8. Distribution and feedback remain separate, optional live stages.

The GitHub replay only validates steps' prepared artifacts. `kind=REPOSITORY_POC_REPLAY` is not a live research run. Keep fresh research runs separately labeled, with provider-call evidence. An Actions failure before persistence may not have a canonical run record; the diagnostics GUI also queries Actions directly for this reason.

## Scheduling

`.github/workflows/weekly-demo.yml` runs Monday at 22:57 UTC, on manual dispatch and source pushes. It commits real run records plus the projection. It does not issue Clay calls or scrape. The original ChatGPT automation remains enabled Monday with its existing America/Los_Angeles context; it performs search-based research and has been told to use this repo after access is verified. Do not create a duplicate paid pipeline.

GitHub scheduled jobs run from the default branch and may be delayed or disabled after inactivity. Check actual Actions evidence and run files. Preserve source changes from automated commits when publishing your own changes; fetch main before writing and use fast-forward-only updates.

## Dashboard and deployment

The public Site loads `dist/data.json` from GitHub main and refreshes every 30 seconds. If GitHub cannot be reached, it uses the hosted snapshot and labels the fallback. Thus data/run commits can update the hosted view without a Sites redeploy. UI code changes still require redeployment.

The week selector filters execution history; tender/partner views show the current dataset, not a reconstructed historical snapshot. Future weeks have no invented runs. Run diagnostics include source revision, stage evidence, failure text, canonical file link, JSON export and live Actions status. Anonymous GitHub API checks can be rate-limited; the GUI links directly to Actions on failure.

GitHub Pages is optional. Choose Pages source “GitHub Actions” and set `ENABLE_GITHUB_PAGES=true` only if using the separate Pages deployment. The public Sites URL remains the primary demo.

Existing Sites identity for owner-authorized redeployment: `appgprj_6a9bd9ac4dec8191b26c539730139b17`. Do not create another Site. The Sites source repository is distinct from GitHub; GitHub export excludes the platform-specific `.openai/hosting.json`. In a host with Sites tools, call get-site for this exact identity, obtain an ephemeral source credential, stage the GitHub checkout with its existing hosting manifest, push exact source, package static `dist/` and deploy a saved version to its current public audience. Never put source credentials into Git.

## Verification and maintenance

```sh
python scripts/validate.py
node --check dist/app.js
python -m unittest discover -s integrations -p 'test_*.py'
python scripts/build_dashboard.py
```

`python scripts/record_execution.py` records an actual replay, including validation and JS syntax checks. It must not be used simply to populate a chart. Preserve failed records. All public-source commits should retain the validation boundary: no direct personal/business emails in public data, no private UUID mappings, no secrets/raw Clay exports.

Update this handover, readiness evidence and relevant execution logs as reality changes. Do not claim account-level spend enforcement, automatic scraping, delivery or partner willingness without evidence.

## Manual publication from an authenticated checkout

Download `source.tar.gz` from the dashboard. It contains public source only, without Git history or hosting credentials. In an environment whose GitHub connection has write permission:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/az2kxx/gtmtechweek.git
cd gtmtechweek
tar -xzf /absolute/path/to/source.tar.gz
python scripts/validate.py
node --check dist/app.js
git add .
git commit -m 'Publish tender PoC, diagnostics and handover'
git push origin main
```

Inspect the push-triggered Actions run; update `config/readiness.json` to reflect actual publication and execution evidence, regenerate `dist/data.json`, and commit that update. Change the repository status text in `dist/app.js` when publication succeeds. UI changes need a Sites redeployment; data-only changes refresh from GitHub. The source archive is a handover snapshot, not an auto-updating backup.
